meta.name: Operational Dashboard
meta.description: Decision-oriented dashboard that prioritizes critical attention, grouped metrics, filters, analytical context, and actionable work.

purpose: Help users understand current operational conditions, identify exceptions, compare meaningful metrics, and choose the next action without displaying every available number at equal prominence.
useWhen: The user must monitor several related operational indicators.
The screen must help prioritize work or identify exceptions.
Metrics require grouping by business meaning.
The screen combines summary information with actionable queues or drill-downs.
doNotUseWhen: The user is primarily locating individual records.
The screen contains only one or two static statistics.
The dominant task is editing one entity.
Cards are being used only because a dashboard appears visually attractive.

selectionQuestions: What decision must the dashboard help the user make?
Which metrics are critical, financial, operational, quality, or informational?
Which indicators require comparison periods or trends?
How fresh must each data source be?
Which filters affect every dashboard region?

regions.name: Page Header
regions.role: Orient the user, state dashboard scope, expose freshness, and present limited page-level actions.
prohibitedComponents: Every export format as a primary button

compact.layout: Stack title, scope, freshness, and primary action.

medium.layout: Title and context left; compact actions right or below.

wide.notes: Keep dashboard content visible without excessive scrolling.

ultrawide.notes: Do not enlarge the title merely because more width exists.

rules: The page header does not contain dashboard metrics.
Refresh and freshness are visually distinct.
Exports are secondary or overflow actions.
Date scope must be explicit when metrics depend on a period.

regions.name: Critical Attention
regions.role: Surface exceptions, deadlines, failures, or risks requiring immediate user attention.
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible only when critical or actionable exceptions exist.

compact.notes: Do not hide critical issues in horizontal carousels.

medium.notes: Each critical item must expose a clear next action.

wide.layout: One prominent summary or constrained alert grid.
wide.notes: Do not compete with several equally red panels.

rules: Only actionable or materially risky conditions appear in this region.
Critical meaning uses text and icon in addition to color.
The region disappears when no critical condition exists.
Do not display neutral empty state as a critical alert.

regions.name: Global Dashboard Filters
regions.role: Control the shared scope of dashboard metrics and analytical regions.
prohibitedComponents: Independent filters that affect only one distant widget without clear labeling
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible when users can meaningfully change dashboard scope.

compact.placement: Compact trigger and active-filter summary below critical attention.
compact.layout: Filter trigger opens a drawer; active filters remain visible.
compact.notes: Do not render a large vertical filter form before dashboard content.

medium.notes: Low-frequency filters may remain inside a drawer.

ultrawide.layout: Horizontal filter bar with constrained control widths.
ultrawide.notes: Do not stretch selects across unused space.

rules: Shared filters must affect clearly identified dashboard regions.
URL state owns shareable date ranges and filters.
Changing filters resets incompatible drill-down state.
Active filters remain visible outside compact drawers.

regions.name: Primary Metrics
regions.role: Present the smallest set of decision-critical metrics grouped by business meaning.
prohibitedComponents: Large grid of equally prominent values
regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible when authoritative metric data is available.

compact.notes: Do not use horizontal metric carousels for critical information.

medium.layout: Two-column metric grid grouped by semantic category.

wide.layout: Up to four metric columns per semantic group.
wide.notes: Group critical, financial, operational, and quality metrics.

ultrawide.layout: Four to six columns only when card content remains readable.
ultrawide.notes: Do not expand to many columns merely to fill width.

rules: Each metric belongs to a documented semantic group.
Metrics include comparison or context when raw values are ambiguous.
Zero, unavailable, and not-calculated values are visually distinct.
Metric cards do not all use the primary accent.

regions.name: Analytical Content
regions.role: Provide charts, distributions, trends, and comparisons that explain metric movement or composition.
prohibitedComponents: Chart without a user decision or explanatory purpose
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible when analytical context materially improves interpretation.

compact.layout: Single-column analytical panels with simplified legends.
compact.notes: Charts must remain readable and may switch to an accessible table summary.

medium.layout: Single or two-column grid based on chart complexity.
medium.notes: Avoid compressing complex charts into narrow columns.

wide.layout: Two-column analytical grid with explicit panel hierarchy.
wide.notes: A dominant chart may span both columns.

ultrawide.layout: Two or three analytical columns according to data complexity.
ultrawide.notes: Do not reduce chart height below readability requirements.

rules: Every chart must have a title, context, and accessible interpretation.
Charts do not duplicate metric cards without adding explanation.
Color is not the only encoding.
Unknown or incomplete data is communicated.

regions.name: Action Queue
regions.role: Translate dashboard insight into prioritized records or tasks requiring user action.
prohibitedComponents: All records from the underlying collection
Bulk destructive actions without an explicit workflow
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible when the dashboard supports a clear next-work decision.

compact.placement: Below analytical content or immediately after metrics when more important.
compact.layout: Prioritized stacked list with essential metadata.
compact.notes: Use a separate searchable-list route for the full collection.

wide.layout: Compact table or split prioritized queues.
wide.notes: Provide a clear route to the full list.

ultrawide.notes: Do not fill extra width with low-priority columns.

rules: Queue ordering reflects an approved operational priority.
The dashboard queue is a curated subset, not a replacement for full search.
Each item provides the minimum context required to act.
View-all navigation preserves relevant dashboard filters when appropriate.

composition.columnPolicy: Regions define their own constrained grids; the page does not use one universal card grid.
spacingOwnership: The dashboard recipe owns spacing between major regions.
MetricGroup owns spacing between semantic metric groups.
Analytical panels own their internal padding.
The action queue owns row and item spacing.
surfacePolicy: Page header and metric grid may render directly on the canvas.
Charts and queues may use distinct surfaces when they form interaction boundaries.
Critical attention uses semantic critical styling.
Do not wrap the complete dashboard in one additional card.
rules: Critical attention precedes ordinary metrics.
Metrics are grouped by business meaning.
Analytical panels explain rather than duplicate metrics.
Action queues connect insight to the next task.
prohibited: A single grid containing every metric with equal prominence.
Charts added without a documented decision purpose.
Large blank dashboard regions reserved for hypothetical future data.
Fixed-height cards that clip long content.

actions.primaryPlacement: Page header when one clear dashboard-level action exists; otherwise inside the relevant action queue.
actions.secondaryPlacement: Page header overflow, panel headers, or contextual drill-down links.
actions.destructivePlacement: Not presented as a dashboard-level primary action.
actions.bulkPlacement: Only inside an explicit action queue with selection and permission context.
actions.contextualPlacement: Metric drill-down, chart exploration, and queue item actions.
actions.overflowPolicy: Exports, configuration, and low-frequency utilities move to the page-header overflow menu.
actions.compactBehavior: Preserve one primary action; move exports and utilities into overflow.
rules: The dashboard must not expose several equally dominant actions.
Metric cards are not buttons unless drill-down behavior is explicit.
Destructive actions require navigation to or opening of an appropriate workflow.

content.headingPolicy: One h1 in the page header; each metric group, analytical section, and queue uses an h2 or appropriately nested heading.
content.longContentPolicy: Metric labels and queue content must support realistic domain lengths without fixed-height clipping.
content.truncationPolicy: Truncate only secondary content and provide full-value access when the value affects decisions.
content.emptyStatePlacement: An entirely empty dashboard explains missing configuration or data source status; individual empty panels remain local.
content.loadingStrategy: Use stable region skeletons for initial loading, preserve populated regions during background refresh, and show local refresh indicators.
content.errorScope: Widget failures remain local when other dashboard regions can still operate; shared filter or authorization failures may affect the route.
rules: Freshness is visible when stale data changes interpretation.
Zero and unavailable values are distinct.
Use realistic financial and operational formatting.
Do not use lorem ipsum or generic metric names.

responsive.minimumViewport: 320 CSS pixels with reduced simultaneous analytical content.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The dashboard must remain usable at 125% browser zoom.
responsive.internalOverflowPolicy: Tables may use controlled horizontal scrolling; charts must resize or switch representation.

transformations.change: Reduce analytical columns before shrinking chart content below readability limits.
transformations.reason: Chart comprehension is more important than filling every column.

transformations.change: Primary metric groups move from up to four columns to two columns; complex analytical panels span full width.
transformations.reason: Preserve readable labels, values, and chart legends.

transformations.change: Metrics become one-column groups, filters move to a drawer, analytical panels stack, and the action queue uses essential metadata only.
transformations.reason: Compact layouts cannot sustain simultaneous metric, filter, and table density.

states.rendering: Render region-shaped skeletons preserving the expected dashboard hierarchy.
states.notes: Do not render identical card skeletons when regions have different structures.

states.rendering: Preserve existing data and show freshness or local refresh indicators.
states.userAction: Continue working or wait for refreshed values.

states.rendering: Render critical attention, metrics, analytical panels, and action queues according to available data.
Explain whether no source data, no configuration, or no activity exists.
states.userAction: Configure, import, change scope, or wait according to product context.

states.rendering: Render successful regions and isolate unavailable or failed widgets.
states.userAction: Continue using available information or retry the failed region.

states.rendering: Render local recovery when one widget fails; route-level recovery when shared dependencies fail.
states.userAction: Retry or contact support using safe details.

states.rendering: Render an approved permission state or omit restricted dashboard sections according to disclosure policy.
Keep data visible with an explicit freshness warning when it remains useful.
Explain that the data source or calculation is unavailable without representing it as zero.
states.userAction: Retry later or inspect source status.

landmarkMap: Page content uses one main landmark inherited from the application shell.
Dashboard groups use labeled section elements.
Global filters use a labeled form landmark when applicable.
Critical attention uses an appropriate alert or labeled section pattern.
headingStructure: Metric groups, analytical sections, and action queues use h2 headings.
Panel titles use h3 only when nested inside an h2 section.
keyboard: All filter controls and chart alternatives are keyboard accessible.
Queue row actions follow table or list keyboard semantics.
announcements: Material filter-result changes should be perceivable without excessive live announcements.
Critical state changes require appropriate status communication.
Background refresh should not repeatedly interrupt assistive technology.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Metric status, chart series, trends, and critical states use labels, icons, patterns, or shapes in addition to color.
rules: Charts require accessible summaries or equivalent data access.
Metric cards must have meaningful labels.
Do not use color-only positive and negative indicators.

prohibitedPatterns: Every available metric displayed at equal prominence.
Horizontal metric carousels containing critical data.
A separate card around every small value.
Raw timestamps or backend metric identifiers.
Critical alerts rendered as ordinary informational cards.
dataMagnitude: The recipe supports a small curated set of top-level metrics rather than unlimited cards.
Action queues represent a prioritized subset of a larger collection.
Metric labels and values must support realistic localization and number lengths.
performance: Avoid rerendering every dashboard region for one local interaction.
Charts should not load heavy libraries when an accessible table or compact visualization is sufficient.
implementation: Use TanStack Query for server state.
Use URL state for shareable global filters.
Use semantic status and chart tokens.
Use project-approved chart components and accessible alternatives.
Machine presence conditions come from presenceDefaults; visibilityCondition prose is explanatory only.

presenceDefaults.rationale: Operational dashboards always require orientation, scope, and freshness context.
Critical attention disappears when there are no actionable or materially risky conditions.
Global filter chrome exists only when users can meaningfully alter shared dashboard scope.
Primary metrics are structural to the dashboard and remain present to render honest zero, unavailable, or not-calculated states.
Analytical panels appear only when the product defines analytical context that adds explanatory value.
An action queue exists only when the dashboard is designed to support a next-work decision; its own empty state may still communicate that no work is pending.

checks.description: The dashboard recipe must validate against the layout recipe schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing recipe fields.

checks.description: Every primary metric must belong to an approved semantic group and support a user decision.
checks.remediation: Remove, regroup, or demote metrics that do not support the primary task.

checks.description: Metric grids, filters, charts, and queues must not create page-level horizontal overflow.
checks.remediation: Correct responsive transformations or internal overflow ownership.

checks.description: Zero, unavailable, stale, and not-calculated values must remain distinguishable.
checks.remediation: Correct value presentation and state semantics.

checks.description: The dashboard should not contain visually prominent but non-actionable decoration.
checks.remediation: Remove or demote content without operational purpose.

checks.description: Dashboard optional regions must follow typed availability/capability signals while primary metrics retain an honest empty or unavailable region.
checks.remediation: Correct craftDefaults/presenceDefaults and keep conditional regions required=false with cardinality.minimum=0.

examples.name: Legal operations dashboard
examples.description: Critical deadlines, financial exposure, operational metrics, case distribution, and a prioritized action queue.

examples.name: Infrastructure operations dashboard
examples.description: Service health, active incidents, capacity indicators, trends, and actionable alerts.
